headline: Highest risk is medium: no documented shared channels or data flows, so prompt injection, leakage, and cascading errors are not evidenced for mem0 + taipy.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: mem0 and taipy expose no documented shared communication channel, filesystem bridge, or MCP/clipboard path in the profiles. With both network_egress set to none and no io_surfaces listed, a prompt-injection pathway between them is not evidenced. Uncertainty is low enough to keep this at none rather than speculate.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or message queue is later configured between mem0 and taipy, reassess injection risk.
IF either agent begins parsing the other's raw text as instructions, the pathway becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated with no shared workspace.
Do not route raw outputs from one agent into the other's instruction channel.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to any bridged messages.
requires-engineering: enforce allowlisted message schemas between components.

B_data_leakage.rationale: The profiles show no touched data classes, no permissions requested, and no shared workspace or authenticated principal. mem0 and taipy both report network_egress none, so there is no documented path for one agent to exfiltrate the other's data. This is provably unexposed from the supplied profiles.
conditions: IF either agent is connected to a shared workspace containing sensitive files, leakage risk must be re-evaluated.
IF network egress is enabled for either agent, data exfiltration pathways may appear.
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of any shared directory.
Leave network egress disabled for both agents.
Separate credentials and OAuth principals if either agent is later granted access.
requires-engineering: add per-agent data-loss-prevention controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: No overlapping write surface is documented: both profiles have empty io_surfaces, empty permissions_requested, and empty concurrency_model. mem0 is knowledge-management and taipy is data-engineering, but the profiles do not show shared mutable resources. Without a shared write target, capability conflict is not evidenced.
conditions: IF both agents are later pointed at the same writable directory or database, conflict risk becomes plausible.
IF either agent is granted git or filesystem write permissions, reassess for race conditions.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Avoid granting write permissions unless required.
Run only one writer per resource at a time.
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared mutable store.

D_cascading_error.rationale: There is no evidence that taipy consumes mem0 outputs as authoritative input, nor that either agent has downstream action-taking authority in the profiles. With no documented pipeline, the cascade from mem0 to taipy is not established. I therefore rate this none rather than infer a hidden orchestration path.
conditions: IF taipy is configured to execute actions directly from mem0-generated text, cascading error risk appears.
IF mem0 outputs are used as unverified facts in a downstream workflow, reassess severity.
mitigations: Insert a human verification step before any action.
Require schema validation on mem0 outputs before taipy consumes them.
Log and review any automated decisions.
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds and rejection rules.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented for either mem0 or taipy. Both profiles are open-source with docs-only evidence and no data classes touched, so there is no compliance pathway to compare. Because the relevant compliance attributes are absent, the safest supported verdict is none.
conditions: IF either agent is later assigned regulated data classes such as PHI or EU PII, compliance review is required.
IF deployment regions or retention policies diverge, reassess compliance impact.
mitigations: Document data classes before deployment.
Keep regulated data out of the pair until policies are defined.
Review retention settings for any shared storage.
requires-engineering: map residency and retention controls explicitly.
